p00002.statement: Infinity is incoherent in both forms, as an ontological posit. The actual: no coherent model is exhibited — the completed totality forbids its own totality as an object, its antinomies are fenced and never resolved, its consistency unprovable from within (Gödel II): the reductio with the four-class catalogue (5-red, Prop. 9). The potential: the undeclared freshness posit, never registered: the idleness theorem and the truthmaker audit (29-fin). The successor act wraps (A7); the schema over finite instances is retained. Not claimed: $0=1$ in ZFC. The incompleteness face: 25-göd.
p00002.source:
5-red ¶, 29-fin
no witness
refs: A7

p00003.statement: The totality has no outside and is unique, so it is complete (observers are shells embedded within, not parallel carriers).

p00010.statement: Realisation, not correspondence: a sufficiently expressive, predictive, registration-complete structure is its subject, not an abstraction of it; by P2 no registration reaches an unregistered reality, so a distinction with no registered residue is no distinction. Identification rows (R) are therefore constitutive: defended by the totality of registered consequences, killed by explicit falsifiers, never interpretive addenda.

p00011.statement: All numbers are unframed Carrier residues, becoming framed rationals ($\fQ$) by a Subject frame — the native arena, in which every structure the sciences use is built exactly (the residue life); the continuum is the metric life of the same objects, a labelled idealisation read against $\mathbb R$ [chart], entered nowhere as an object. The accessible smalls are the natural counts below the observer’s horizon, the wrap-free window of primality, parity and order; everything beyond is hard at its scale (B8, B9).

p00015.statement: The substrate residue: the quarter-turn ($4\mid\Om-1$, B3) and the triality centre ($3\mid\Om+1$, B4) jointly hold iff $\Om\equiv5\pmod{12}$ — the arithmetic shadow of the four-fold and the cubic, one in each frame torus. Both are relations certified by realisations, never properties of an integer: $Q_4$ by the quantum realisation (D4), the triality centre by the strong realisation (D6); the inference runs structure $\to$ congruence. There is no population of candidate $\Om$ (A3); a laboratory pattern instantiates the residue or does not (C13).

p00017.statement: Physical constants are definite Carrier residues, $\Om$-hard to every bounded observer: the register $\{\dS,\Om,c,\hbar,G,k_B\}$ is generator-free in $\dS$ alone — $G=2\dS=-c^2$, $c^2=2^{-1}$, $\hbar^2=-1$, $k_B^2=-2$, $|k_B|=\hbar/c$; the defining congruences are the observer’s complete certificates, $G$ exact, the rest up to sign (B10); $h\equiv-\hbar$ is the per-cycle rebooking (D7). No Subject counterpart of $G$ or $\hbar$; no fifth constant (C1). Orientation C7; hardness B8.

refs: B8, B10, C1, C7, D7

p00018.statement: The two-level horizon law: hardness is one mechanism at every scale — $\Om$-hard when the role lives at the Carrier’s scale, $\p $-hard when beyond the Subject’s own horizon $\sqrt{\p }$ inside its own shell; hardness attaches to roles, never bare residues. The saturating Subject ($\p ^2\to\Om$) locks the ladder $\mathrm{small}<\Om^{1/4}<\p\text{-hard}<\Om^{1/2}<\Om\text{-hard}<\Om$, one square-root horizon per embedding. Certification: B9. Lab-verified ($\Om=2{,}408{,}561$).

p00019.statement: Certification is the orthogonal axis to the B8 bands: a certified entity carries a bounded-height defining relation holding across shells; a framed transcendental is a hard role with none. Registers: at the Carrier the four constants (B7); at the Subject the half-period and quarter-turn, $2\pi\equiv-1$, $i^2\equiv-1$ (C1) — the same congruence shapes (self-similarity). Physical constants $\Om$-hard, mathematical constants $\p $-hard.

p00020.statement: One gauge bit closes the sign sector: no C14-type marker exists — $-1$ is a square on admissible $\Om$, so square class is pair-blind, and integer parity is chart data (A8). Registered faces are pair-invariant: $c^2$, the one-way member synchronisation gauge (C8); $|k_B|$ (C12); $\{\hbar,h\}$ the two named unit faces (B7). Shell data, capacity-first: $\kap $ primitive, $\p =4\kap +1$, $i=-\gen^\kap $ (C7), $\pi=2\kap $, $e=\gen^{\,i}$; $\gen$ the one nonsquare frame datum (C3, C8). The web closes on every shell: $2\pi\equiv-1$, $\gen^{\,\pi}\equiv-1$, $-\pi=2^{-1}$. The constants: B7; the continuum $\pi$ a labelled chart constant (N2).

p00026.statement: One frame group, three sectors: gravity’s $(3{+}1)$ tensor, the Riemann observer geometry, and the quantum spinor structure are three readings of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\Om)$ — its three tori the scale-time, translation, and boost freedoms, its order $(\Om{-}1)\Om(\Om{+}1)$ the observer variety — the norm-one quaternion sphere is $\mathrm{SL}_2$ itself, the spin cover of the rotation group $\mathrm{PGL}_2\cong\mathrm{SO}_3$ that carries the cone chart (C22); continuum shadow the de Sitter $S^3$, a declared chart (C23) — its spinor double cover the Clifford layer (D4). Falsifier: a registered space-time, observer, or spinor freedom outside the three tori of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\Om)$ — a fifth force or an extra dimension.

p00027.statement: Orientation is derived, not conventional: the $c$-square congruence ($\dS$ even, C8) annihilates orientation transport on every Carrier carrying it ($i^{\dS}\in\{\pm1\}$); pullback covariance and count positivity fix the oriented quarter-turn $i=-\gen^\kap $; the joint flip $(\gen,i,s)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-i,-s)$ preserves every registered count — the matter–antimatter gauge, selected factually by the instance’s matter content. The constants’ derivation consumes no selection (B7). Parity marker: C14. Sector faces: H2, K1–K3.

p00028.statement: The square class is chronon parity: for a primitive drive the squares are $\langle \gen^2\rangle$ — a residue’s quadratic class is its drive-step parity. Registered transport is even, the one-way multiplier $\gen$ odd: the one-way speed is gauge, the two-way constant invariant ($[c^2]$ even iff $\dS$ even — the $c$-square congruence, a relation certified by the unit realisation D7, not a property of the integer $\dS$). The second unit marker (order two, D7); the Tsirelson $\sqrt2=\zeta_8+\zeta_8^{-1}$ its two-way symmetrisation.

The momentum reading is one quarter-turn from the winding, $p=i\,k$; the canonical commutator $[\hat q,\hat p]=i\hbar$ composes the Subject’s chart quarter-turn with the Carrier’s action quantum (D7, B7).

The strata coincide exactly on the stationary core-valued $Q_4$ sector; two proved reductions connect them, and the residual realisation content is the stratum-sampling clause (D10); on a single Object the theorem’s weights are uniform over the fibres (22-qm Rem. borndomain), non-uniform statistics arriving through the engineered-core readout. Witnesses and readout: 22-qm.

The minimal laboratory pattern with the quarter-turn core, the triality centre and the $c$-square (B5) and the Subject resolvable ($\p^2<\Om$) is $(13,233)$ by exhaustive scan — host-decided, not a predicate the physical Carrier passes.

The dichotomy is the fold congruence $3\kap r+4s\equiv1\ (\mathrm{mod}\ 4\kap )$, solvable iff $\kap$ odd.

For every odd $\p$, $G\cong\mathbb{P}^1\times\F_\p\times C_{\p -1}$: one direction, one shell cell, one drive phase. Two fibrations share the count: non-split $C_{\p +1}$ over $\p (\p -1)$ with the cone-chart section (C19); split $C_{\p -1}$ over $\p (\p +1)$ without (40-hyper B2). Decides Y4.

p00137.statement: The spatial chart is the 3-sphere (declared): the frame torsor $\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\Om)$ (C6) carries one form on every shell — $\mathrm{SU}_2(\F_{\p^2}/\F_\p)=\mathrm{SL}_2(\F_\p)$ for the Hermitian form $wJ$, $w^{\p}=-w$ — with the three element types of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$, of which $SU(2)$ has one, all of finite order, and the sphere $x^2+y^2+z^2+w^2=1$ and $ad-bc=1$ one quadric of $\p^3-\p$ points through the quarter-turn: the compact real form is no datum of the finite structure and cycle closure selects nothing. $SU(2)=S^3$ is declared the continuum chart of the frame torsor [chart]; given it, the spinor sign gives $S^3$ rather than $SO(3)$ (C22), uniqueness is Poincaré–Perelman [import], and the global de Sitter slicing has $S^3$ sections [import], the chart fixing $\Om\sim10^{122}$.

p00138.statement: The third-order wall of $\pi$: for every prime $\p\ge5$, $\sigma_\p=\sum_{k<(\p-1)/2}\binom{2k}{k}/((2k+1)16^{k})$ satisfies $\sigma_\p\equiv0\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{2})$ (Sun, JNT 131 (2011), (1.4)) and $\sigma_\p/\p^{2}\equiv(-1)^{(\p+1)/2}B_{\p-3}/36\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p)$: Sun’s Conjecture 5.1, $\sigma_\p\equiv(-1)^{(\p-1)/2}(H_{\p-1}/12+3\p^{4}B_{\p-5}/160)\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{5})$ for $\p>5$, proved by Hessami Pilehrood, Hessami Pilehrood and Tauraso (Int. J. Number Theory 8 (2012), Thm. 5 (44)), reduced mod $\p^{3}$ with Glaisher’s $H_{\p-1}\equiv-\p^{2}B_{\p-3}/3\ (\mathrm{mod}\ \p^{3})$; $\p=5$ direct. Re-verified for all primes below $10^{4}$.

p00139.statement: The horizon is the origin’s antipode on the boost torus: for $w^2= u$ a nonsquare (the drive $\gen$ serves), the torsor identification $\mathbb{P}^1(\F_\p)\cong C_{\p +1}$ based at the origin — $P\mapsto u_P/ ar u_P$, $u_P$ the unique boost carrying $0$ to $P$ — is equivariant, sends the origin to $1$ and the horizon class $[1{:}0]$ to $-1=\zeta^{(\p +1)/2}$; $\{ ext{origin}, ext{horizon}\}$ is the sign pair $C_{\p -1}\cap C_{\p +1}$ (C20), exchanged by the torus’s unique involution $q\mapsto u/q$. On the additive cycle the antipode is no residue (1:Z1): the seam between $2\kap$ and $2\kap +1=2^{-1}$, labelled $\p /2$ and charted $\infty$ (1:Z2). Verified at $\p =5,13,17,29,37$ for every nonsquare $ u$ and at every $\p =4\kap +1\le200$.

p00144.statement: The four chains of 13-epi are E- and G-partial sums [import]: the derangement chain $D_n/n!=\sum_{k\le n}(-1)^{k}/k!$ is the partial-sum chain of the E-function $e^{-z}$ at $z=1$; the arcsin and Machin chains are partial-sum chains of the G-functions $\arcsin z$ at $1/2$ and $\arctan z$ at $1/5$, $1/239$; $e^{\pm1}\in\mathcal E$ and $\pi,1/\pi\in\mathcal G$, both rings (Fischler–Rivoal, Comment. Math. Helv. 89 (2014); J. Éc. polytech. Math. 3 (2016), Def. 2). The factorial rate $\Theta(k/\log k)$ against the geometric rate $\Theta(k)$ of 13-epi E5 is the rate of E- against G-partial sums; a factorial-rate chain by rounding, $\mathrm{round}(n!\,x)/n!$, exists for every real $x$ and distinguishes nothing. Whether $\pi$ is the value of an E-function with rational coefficients at a rational point is a question of the continuum, not of the frame: the conjecture $\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal E\cap\operatorname{Frac}\mathcal G=\overline{\Q}$ (ibid. p. 37) would answer it negatively; the split of 13-epi E5 is by kind of chain and needs no such answer.

p01028.source: 6:E2

p01029.statement: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian obstruction: no finite subgroup of $SO(3)$ is an $\varepsilon$-net for $\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0=\arccos\big((3\sqrt5-1)/8\big)\approx44.5^\circ$, the covering radius of the icosahedral group (A3); the tetrahedral, cyclic and dihedral groups have radius $\ge\pi/2$, the octahedral $\approx62.8^\circ$. Finite subgroups cannot approximate $SO(3)$; the window does (Y5).
p01029.source: A3

p01030.statement: Continuous symmetry, the non-abelian case resolved by the window: the framed quaternions $W_H^{4}$, read in a shell $\p>8H^{2}$, compose exactly (products land in $W_{4H^{2}}$); normalised, they are an $\varepsilon$-net of $SO(3)$ with $\varepsilon\le2\arcsin(1/H)$ (round $Hs$ to the lattice). At $H=3$, $\p=73$: $38.9^\circ<\varepsilon_0$, finer than any finite subgroup; measured $30.0^\circ$.
p01030.source: Section 6

p01024.statement: The conjecture of the conclusion, what remains after Y1–Y5: the Lie-algebra layer — one-parameter subgroups and their generators inside the window, where iterating a window rotation $m$ times consumes range as $H^{2m}$; whether the Cayley step of 8-dirac (8:C4) supplies exact one-parameter subgroups of the window net on every shell is open.

p01020.statement: No element of additive order two (Thm. 5.1): $2s=0$ forces $s=0$; the antipode of the origin on the additive cycle is not a residue; it sits between $2\kap=(\p-1)/2$ and $2\kap+1=(\p+1)/2=2^{-1}$ (20-rh B8).

p01021.statement: The antipode named $\infty$: the horizon of the observer at $0$ (00:C25, 00:D13), the compactification point of the framed line [chart]; its reading as classical infinity is the chart, not a residue.
p01021.source:
Section 5.1; 00:C25, 00:D13
master: 00:C25, 00:D13

p02001.statement: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$; its generators are the $\gen^{u}$, $u\in\Zp^{\times}$; $\gen^{(\p-1)/2}=-1$; $-1$ is a square in $\Fp$ iff $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; the fourth roots of unity form the unique subgroup of order four (1:A1, 1:B2).
p02001.source: Rotman; 1:A1; 1:B2

p02002.statement: The sign of the quarter-turn exponent: $\im=\gen^{-\kap}=-\gen^{\kap}$, the exponent negative by pullback covariance (00:C7); the positive-exponent reading is the conjugate chart. Declared here, derived in the corpus.
p02002.source: 00:C7; 1:A2

p02003.statement: Topology: a closed connected surface with Euler characteristic $2$ is the two-sphere; the suspension of a circle is $S^{2}$ (Hatcher, Ex. 0.14); a quotient of a regular CW complex by a subcomplex is a CW complex.

p02004.statement: The framed-rational charts of 1-algebra: on one shell the scale grids $x/\gen^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, trade range for resolution (1:D5); across shells the tower resolves every real (1:Y2).
p02004.source: 1:D5; 1:Y2

p02005.statement: The shell $(\kap,\Fp)$, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$ prime; the half-period $\pi:=2\kap$; the meridian steps $I_{\p}=\{0,\dots,\pi\}$; the phase cycle $\Phi_{\p}\cong C_{\p-1}$, $m\mapsto\gen^{m}$ (Defs. 2.1, 2.5; 00:C1).

p02006.statement: The frame $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$: origin, unit, and the Subject’s drive generator $\gen$, a primitive generator of $\Fpx$; $\chron$ the chronon (00:C1, convention 3).
p02006.source:
Def. 2.3; 00:C1
master: 00:C1

p02007.statement: Primitive generators form one orbit: every generator is $\gen^{u}$ with $u\in\Zp^{\times}$, a torsor for $\operatorname{Aut}(C_{\p-1})$ (Props. 2.7, 4.5).
p02007.source: A1

p02008.statement: Cellular automorphisms of the index grid: $m\mapsto\pm m+c$, the dihedral group of the phase cycle; on the completion also meridian reversal $a\mapsto\pi-a$, exchanging the poles. The reindexing $\rho_{u}\colon m\mapsto um$ preserves latitude adjacency only for $u\equiv\pm1\pmod{\p-1}$; $\sigma$ is not a map of $\Sp$ ($\north$ one vertex, $L_{\pi}$ has $\p-1$); decided on $\p\le29$.
p02008.source: Prop. 2.8

p02009.statement: The orbital shell $\Sp$: vertices $\north$ and $v_{a,m}$ ($1\le a\le\pi$, $m\in\Phi_{\p}$), meridian and latitude edges, north triangles, quadrilaterals (Def. 3.1). The action reading $v_{a,m}\equiv a\gen^{m}$ is $\pi$-to-one onto $\Fpx$: the surface is two-faced (00:B11, 1:C4).
p02009.source: Def. 3.1; 1:C4

p02010.statement: Counts: $|V|=\pi(\p-1)+1$, $|E|=2\pi(\p-1)$, $|F|=\pi(\p-1)$, $\chi(\Sp)=1$; the completion has $(\pi-1)(\p-1)+2$ vertices, $(2\pi-1)(\p-1)$ edges, $\pi(\p-1)$ faces, $\chi=2$ (Rem. 3.4).

p02011.statement: Canonical spherical completion: collapsing $L_{\pi}$ to $\south$ gives a closed orientable surface — every edge in two faces, every vertex link a cycle — with $\chi=2$, hence $S^{2}$ (A3), on every shell (Thm. 3.3; decided on $\p\in\{5,13,17,29\}$ by exhaustive incidence).
p02011.source: A3

p02012.statement: Frame covariance: $\Sp$ is one complex for every generator — the index grid $I_{\p}\times\Phi_{\p}$ with its step relations; the frame $\gen'=\gen^{u}$ moves the field labels, $a\gen^{m}\mapsto a\gen^{um}$, by the automorphism $\rho_{u}$ of $\Phi_{\p}$, not the cells. The map $\varphi_{u}$ of Prop. 3.5 is cellular only for $u\equiv\pm1$.
p02012.source: Prop. 3.5

p02013.statement: The half-period: $\gen^{\pi}=-1$ for every primitive $\gen$, $\pi=2\kap$ (Prop. 4.1); $2\pi\equiv-1$ (00:C1).

p02014.statement: The quarter-turn subgroup $\Qp=\{x:x^{4}=1\}$ is the unique subgroup of order four; $\gen^{\kap}$ has order four with $(\gen^{\kap})^{2}=-1$; $\Qp=\{\pm1,\pm\im\}$ (Def. 4.2, Prop. 4.3; 1:B2).

p02015.statement: The oriented quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^{\kap}=\gen^{-\kap}$, $\im^{2}=-1$, orientation by A2 (Rem. 4.6); on $\F_{13}(\chron;0,1,2)$: $\im=5$, $-\im=8$, $\pi=6$ [value] (Fig. 3).
p02015.source:
A2
master: 00:C5

p02016.statement: The exponential unit $\eu:=\gen^{\im}$, $\im$ read as an exponent in $\Phi_{\p}$ through its residue representative; derived, generator-dependent (Rem. 4.7; 00:C1, convention 3); on $\F_{13}$, $\eu=6=\pi$ [value].
p02016.source: Section 4; 00:C1

p02017.statement: Orientation classes: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $\im'=-\gen'^{\kap}$ equals $\im$ when $u\equiv1\pmod4$ and $-\im$ when $u\equiv3\pmod4$; the oriented quarter-turn is frame-covariant within one class of generators, not under every generator change.
p02017.source: Rem. 4.11

p02018.statement: The Euler identity on the shell: $\eu^{\im\pi}=\gen^{2\kap\im^{2}}=(-1)^{\im}$, equal to $-1$ exactly when the representative of $\im$ is odd (00:C14); the oriented frames of a shell are those with $-\gen^{\kap}$ odd — on $\F_{13}$, $\gen=2$ ($\im=5$) is one, on $\F_{17}$, $\gen=3$ ($\im=4$) is not.
p02018.source:
Section 4; 00:C14
master: 00:C14

p02019.statement: Negation $R(x)=-x$ and inversion $I(x)=x^{-1}$ are commuting involutions; off $\Qp$ the $\langle R,I\rangle$-orbit $\{x,-x,x^{-1},-x^{-1}\}$ has four elements, and $\Fpx\setminus\Qp$ splits into $\kap-1$ such orbits (Props. 4.8, 4.9; 1:B2).
p02019.source: 1:B2

p02020.statement: Euclidean conjugation $C_{\gen}\colon(a,b)\mapsto(a,-b)$ is an involution of the coordinate pairs $\Fp^{2}$; on the shell $a+b\im$ is a field element and the pair map $\Fp^{2}\to\Fp$ is $\p$-to-one (1:E2), so $C_{\gen}$ is a chart-level involution, not a field automorphism.
p02020.source: Prop. 4.13; 1:E2

p02021.statement: The comparison map $\Xi_{\p,\gen}$ [chart]: $\north\mapsto(0,0,1)$, $v_{a,m}\mapsto(\sin\theta_{a}\cos\phi_{m},\sin\theta_{a}\sin\phi_{m},\cos\theta_{a})$ with $\theta_{a}=\pi_{\R}a/(2\kap)$, $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/(\p-1)$, $\pi_{\R}$ the chart constant (00:N2); $L_{\pi}\mapsto(0,0,-1)$ (Def. 5.1).
p02021.source: Def. 5.1; 00:N2

p02022.statement: Base-grid estimate [chart]: every point of $S^{2}$ lies within geodesic distance $\sqrt2\,\pi_{\R}/(\p-1)$ of $\Xi_{\p,\gen}(V(\Sp))$; measured covering radius $0.360$ at $\p=13$ against the bound $0.370$ (Prop. 5.2).

p02023.statement: Fixed-shell refinement is bounded: with $m=\lfloor\log_{\gen}(2\kap+1)\rfloor$ no point $x/\gen^{n}$, $|x|\le2\kap$, lies in $(\max(1-\gen^{-m},2\kap\gen^{-m-1}),1)$ at any depth, so the covering radius of the scale grid in $[0,1]$ is $\ge\tfrac12\min(\gen^{-m},1-2\kap\gen^{-m-1})$ for every $N$: $1/8$ at $(13,2)$, $5/22$ at $(13,11)$.
p02023.source: Section 5

p02024.statement: Finite precision across the tower [chart]: for every $L$-bounded observable family, $\varepsilon>0$ and configuration on $(S^{2})^{r}$ some shell $\p$ carries grid points within $\varepsilon$ (1:Y2 with the path bound of E2); on one shell the precision is bounded by E3.
p02024.source: Thm. 5.7; 1:Y2

p02025.statement: $\gen$ is a principal $n$-th root of unity, $n=\p-1$: $\gen^{n}=1$, $\sum_{j<n}\gen^{jk}=0$ for $0<k<n$, and $n^{-1}=-1$ in $\Fp$ (Prop. 6.1; $2\pi\equiv-1$).

p02026.statement: The ring Fourier transform on the phase cycle: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=\sum_{j<n}v_{j}\gen^{jk}$ on $V_{\gen}=\Fp^{n}$; the matrix $(W_{\gen})_{kj}=\gen^{jk}$ (Def. 6.2, Rem. 6.4).
p02026.source: Def. 6.2

p02027.statement: Inversion: $v_{j}=-\sum_{k<n}\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}\gen^{-jk}$, i.e. $W_{\gen}^{-1}=-(\gen^{-jk})_{jk}=-W_{\gen}J$ (Prop. 6.3; 6:B5), exact on every shell.

p02028.statement: Polynomial reading: $\mathcal F_{\gen}(v)_{k}=P_{v}(\gen^{k})$ with $P_{v}=\sum_{j}v_{j}X^{j}$; the transform exchanges coefficients with values on the phase cycle (Prop. 6.5).

p02029.statement: Covariance under generator change: for $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $v^{(\gen')}_{j}=v^{(\gen)}_{uj}$ and $\mathcal F_{\gen'}(v^{(\gen')})=\mathcal F_{\gen}(v^{(\gen)})$ (Prop. 6.7).

p02030.statement: Exact external transport [chart]: $\chi(\gen^{m})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im m/n}$ is an isomorphism of $\Fpx$ onto the complex $n$-th roots of unity with $\chi(\gen^{m+1})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im/n}\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\gen^{m+\pi})=-\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\im\gen^{m})=\im\,\chi(\gen^{m})$, $\chi(\gen^{jr})=e^{-2\pi_{\R}\im jr/n}$ (Prop. 6.8).

p02031.statement: The large-$\p$ reading [chart]: the phase cycle read as the $n$-point grid $\phi_{m}=2\pi_{\R}m/n$ on $S^{1}$; the classical sampled DFT, exact recovery for $n>2N$, and trapezoidal convergence are the degenerate comparison case, imported (Rem. 6.12).

p02034.statement: The observer-local chart: a metric, geodesics and curvature on the completion, in which local Euclidean geometry would be written; deferred by the paper (Discussion, “Boundary of the Approximation Claim”); no Gromov–Hausdorff statement is made or claimed.

p03001.statement: Finite-field algebra: $\Fpx$ is cyclic of order $\p-1$ with two square classes $S=(\Fpx)^{2}$ and $N=\Fpx\setminus S$ of $(\p-1)/2$ each; $-1\in S$ for $\p\equiv1\pmod4$; $X^{2}- u$ is irreducible for $ u\in N$ and $\Fpq=\Fp(\sqrt u)$; every element of $\Fp$ is a square in $\Fpq$.
p03001.source: [Lidl & Niederreiter 1997]; 1:A1

p03002.statement: Quadratic forms over finite fields of odd characteristic: nondegenerate forms are classified by dimension and discriminant, isotropic in dimension three and more; in dimension four the hyperbolic type (discriminant a square, Witt index two, $q^{3}+q^{2}-q$ zeros, $|O_{4}^{+}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{2}-1)^{2}$) and the elliptic type (discriminant a nonsquare, Witt index one, $q^{3}-q^{2}+q$ zeros, $|O_{4}^{-}(q)|=2q^{2}(q^{4}-1)$); Witt’s theorem.
p03002.source: [Lam 2005; Taylor 1992; Grove 2002]

p03003.statement: The framed substrate: the shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with frame $(\chron;0,1,\g)$ and quarter-turn $\im=-\g^{\kap}$ (1:B2, B3); the square class as drive-step parity, the drive $\g$ a nonsquare on every shell, $\nu=\g$ canonical (8:B3, B5; 00:C8); the boost cycle as the non-split torus (8:D5; 22:A2).
p03003.source: [Akhtman 2025]; 8:B3; 00:C3

p03004.statement: The continuum comparison: Minkowski’s form $-c^{2}t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ of signature $(1,3)$ and Witt index one over $\R$, its Lorentz group $O(1,3)$; the ordering of $\R$ that finite fields lack.
p03004.source: [Hawking & Ellis 1973]

p03005.statement: The shell $\Fp$, $\p=4\kap+1$, with its classes $S$, $N$; the diagonal form $Q_{ u}(t,x,y,z)=- u t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$, $ u\in\Fpx$, a form over $\Fp$: Euclidean when $ u\in S$ (all coefficients in one class), Lorentzian when $ u\in N$; $Q_{ u}$ depends on $ u$ only through its class ($ u\mapsto u w^{2}$ is $t\mapsto wt$); $ u=\g$ canonical.
p03005.source: Eq. (1); 8:B2

p03006.statement: Nonexistence of a causal square root: no $c\in\Fp$ has $c^{2}=\nu$ for $\nu\in N$; for $c\in\Fpx$ every coefficient of $-c^{2}t^{2}+x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}$ is a square ($-1=\im^{2}$), the form Euclidean with $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$ zeros; $c=0$ gives a degenerate form.
p03006.source: Thm. 1

p03007.statement: Square-class absorption: if $a_{i}/a_{0}\in S$ for all $\im$ then $Q\simeq a_{0}\sum Y_{i}^{2}$ by $Y_{i}=w_{i}X_{i}$, $w_{i}^{2}=a_{i}/a_{0}$; no root of $a_{0}$ is needed, and none exists for $a_{0}\in N$ ($-a_{0}$ is a nonsquare with it).
p03007.source: Lemma 1

p03008.statement: The dichotomy lives on the shell: $\operatorname{disc}Q_{ u}\equiv u$ (as $-1\in S$); for $ u\in N$ the form is elliptic, Witt index one, with $\p^{3}-\p^{2}+\p$ null points; for $ u\in S$ hyperbolic, Witt index two, $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$; every $ u$ on $\p\le41$ ($2041$ and $2353$ at $13$; 8:B7).
p03008.source:
Section 2
master: 00:C3

p03009.statement: The Witt decomposition: for $ u\in N$ the plane $x^{2}- u t^{2}$ (the norm of $\Fpq$) is anisotropic and $y^{2}+z^{2}=(y+iz)(y-iz)$ hyperbolic, so $Q_{ u}=H\perp\langle1,- u angle$, index one; for $ u=w^{2}$ the $(t,x)$-plane is hyperbolic too, $H\perp H$. Over $\Fpq$, $ u=c^{2}$ and $Q_{ u}\simeq\sum X_{i}^{2}$: hyperbolic ($16\,225$ zeros at $q=25$); the extension dissolves the split.
p03009.source: Cor. 1

p03010.statement: The finite Lorentz group of the shell: $O(Q_{\nu},\Fp)=O_{4}^{-}(\p)$ of order $2\p^{2}(\p^{4}-1)$ ($31\,200$, $9\,653\,280$, $48\,274\,560$ at $5$, $13$, $17$, by frame counting); the Euclidean group $O_{4}^{+}(\p)$ of order $2\p^{2}(\p^{2}-1)^{2}$; over $\Fpq$, $O(Q_{\nu},\Fpq)=O_{4}^{+}(\p^{2})$ ($486\,720\,000$ at $\p=5$): split type means Witt index two.
p03010.source: Section 4

p03011.source: Section 4

p03012.statement: The boost datum: $K=\Fpq=\Fp(\sqrt u)$ with the Frobenius conjugation and the norm $N(\gamma+b\sqrt u)=\gamma^{2}- u b^{2}$; the boost $\Lambda(\gamma,b)= igl( egin{smallmatrix}\gamma&b\ u b&\gamma\end{smallmatrix} igr)$ for $N=1$; the rapidity parameter is a norm-one element of $K^{ imes}$ (8:D4; C5 for $\g^{\Delta m}$).
p03012.source: Section 3; 8:D4

p03013.statement: $\Lambda(\gamma,b)$ preserves $- u t^{2}+x^{2}$ exactly and $\Lambda(z_{1})\Lambda(z_{2})=\Lambda(z_{1}z_{2})$: the boosts are the norm-one cycle $N^{1}\simeq C_{\p+1}$, the non-split torus, and exhaust $SO(Q_{ u},\Fp)$ in dimension $1{+}1$ ($6$, $14$, $18$ at $5$, $13$, $17$); with $ u\in S$ the same construction is the split torus $C_{\p-1}$ — the two tori are the two signatures (00:C3).
p03013.source:
Section 3
master: 00:C3

p03014.statement: Velocity: $\gamma eq0$ on every boost; $v=- u b/\gamma\in\Fp$; $\gamma^{2}( u-v^{2})= u$, the finite $\gamma=1/\sqrt{1- eta^{2}}$ with $ eta^{2}=v^{2}/ u$ ($ eta$ itself is no shell quantity, 8:B8); Einstein’s law $v_{12}=(v_{1}+v_{2})/(1+v_{1}v_{2}/ u)$ exact, the denominator never zero; $v$ is two-to-one on $N^{1}$.
p03014.source: Section 3

p03015.statement: Dimension $1{+}3$: the $x$-boost $\Lambda\oplus I_{2}$ lies in $O(Q_{\nu},\Fp)$; with $O(3,\Fp)$ on $(x,y,z)$, of order $2\p(\p^{2}-1)$, the $x$-boosts generate $O(Q_{\nu},\F_{5})=O_{4}^{-}(5)$ ($31\,200$ elements by closure); over the extension the group is $O_{4}^{+}(\p^{2})$, the Euclidean one (B6).
p03015.source: Section 3

p03016.source: Section 3

p03017.statement: $\F_{13}$ [value]: $S=\{1,3,4,9,10,12\}$, $N=\{2,5,6,7,8,11\}$; $\nu=2=\g$; $X^{2}-2$ irreducible, $c=\sqrt2\in K\setminus\F_{13}$; $2041$ null points of $Q_{2}$ on the shell, $4\,855\,201$ over $K$; $14$ boosts $(\gamma,b)$ with the $7$ velocities $\{0,2,3,6,7,10,11\}$; $\Lambda(u)$ at $u=2$ has $a=-5/(2c)\notin\F_{13}$.
p03017.source: Section 2

p03018.statement: Causality is algebraic and lives on the shell: the time axis is the coordinate carrying the nonsquare class ($\nu=\g$), the null cone and the two non-null classes its invariant separation (B7), the boosts the non-split torus (C2); $\Fpq$ is where $c=\sqrt\nu$ is written and where the dichotomy collapses (B5). Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity (8:B8).
p03018.source:
Section 4; 00:C3
master: 00:C3

p03019.statement: Local correspondence [chart]: integer points with $|Q_{\nu}|<\p$ satisfy $Q_{\nu}=0$ in $\Z$ iff on the shell (the window law, 1:D2); the asymptotic claim of Remark 1 — density and equidistribution of the shell’s null points against the real cone — is not proved and stands as Y1.
p03019.source: Rem. 1; 1:D2

p03022.statement: The large-$\p$ correspondence of Remark 1: whether the window points of the shell’s null cone approach the real light cone with density and equidistribution as $\p\to\infty$; named by the paper as future work, not claimed, no witness.
p03022.source: Rem. 1

p04001.statement: Finite sets and maps: a map between finite sets of equal cardinality is injective exactly when it is bijective; a set of cardinality at most $|U|$ injects into $U$; unique factorisation in $\Z$ (the Gödel code).
p04001.source: standard; [G"odel 1931; Smullyan 1991]

p04002.statement: Sufficiency: minimal sufficient statistics are unique up to bijection; invoked as motivation only — no probability enters, the operative notion is set-theoretic (B3).
p04002.source: [Lehmann & Scheff'e 1950; Keener 2010]

p04003.statement: The corpus: the shell $\Fp$, $\p=4\kap+1$, with its frame and quarter-turn (1:B2, B3); its frames $x\mapsto a+bx$ (1:C2; 00:C1); the Carrier and its readings as incomplete projections (00:A8, A6); finiteness and counting by return (00:A4, A7); $4\mid\p-1$ from the two involutions (00:B3); consolidation as frame maps, innovation as the extension $\Fpq$ where $\sqrt\nu$ is written (3:B5).
p04003.source:
[Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2025]
master: 00:A4, 00:A7, 00:A8

p04004.statement: The empirical record: cross-modal alignment and unsupervised translation between independently trained embeddings; grokking; emergence, transfer under shared structure, latent knowledge, interpolation of arbitrary labels; hyperspherical embeddings; floating point as a finite subset of $\R$; sphere packing.
p04004.source: [Radford et al. 2021; Jha et al. 2025; Power et al. 2022; Wei et al. 2022; Hernandez et al. 2022; Burns et al. 2022; Zhang et al. 2017; Chen et al. 2020; Gao et al. 2021; Ethayarajh 2019; Wang & Isola 2020; Goldberg 1991; Conway & Sloane 1999]

p04005.statement: The latent domain: a finite set $\mathcal Z\subset\mathcal U_t=\Fp$, the complete relational domain a model reconstructs from its data; the shell is the ambient set and a reading of it is a projection (00:A6).
p04005.source:
Def. 1; Section 3
master: 00:A6

p04006.statement: Observation maps: $g_m:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X_m$ deterministic, one per modality, carrying its resolution; no stochastic model and no conditional independence is assumed; every cross-modal relation factors through $\mathcal Z$.
p04006.source: Eq. (2); Eq. (1)

p04007.statement: Adequacy: $E_m:\mathcal X_m\to W_m$ is adequate when $E_m\circ g_m=\varphi_m$ is a bijection $\mathcal Z\to W_m$; minimality, $W_m=\varphi_m(\mathcal Z)$, is part of the bijection, so the minimal adequate representation of Section 2 and Definition 2 are one notion.

p04008.statement: Adequacy makes the observation map injective on the latent domain: $g_m(z)=g_m(z')$ forces $z=z'$; $\mathcal Z$ is the domain modality $m$ resolves completely.
p04008.source: Section 3

p04009.statement: Uniqueness up to bijection: for adequate $E_1$, $E_2$ of one $g$, $\psi=\varphi_2\circ\varphi_1^{-1}:W_1\to W_2$ is a bijection with $E_2\circ g=\psi\circ E_1\circ g$ — $E_2=\psi\circ E_1$ on $g(\mathcal Z)$, on all of $\mathcal X$ when $\mathcal X=g(\mathcal Z)$; $\psi$ is the unique map with this property.
p04009.source: Lemma 2; Lemma 1

p04010.statement: The embedding into the shell: $|W_m|=|\mathcal Z|\le\p$, so an injection $\iota_m:W_m\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ exists — the one place finiteness enters; canonically $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ followed by the inclusion; $\psi_m:=\iota_m\circ\varphi_m:\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ is modality $m$'s chart of $\mathcal Z$.
p04010.source: Section 3

p04011.statement: Theorem 1 (i), (ii): every chart $\psi_m$ is injective, and $\Psi_{m\to n}:=\psi_n\circ\psi_m^{-1}:\psi_m(\mathcal Z)\to\psi_n(\mathcal Z)$ is a well-defined bijection, with $\Psi_{n\to k}\circ\Psi_{m\to n}=\Psi_{m\to k}$ and $\Psi_{m\to m}$ the identity.
p04011.source: Thm. 1

p04012.statement: Theorem 1 (iii): with $\iota_m=\varphi_m^{-1}$ every chart is the inclusion $\mathcal Z\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_t$ and $\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$; canonical structurally (unique once $\mathcal Z$ is fixed), not algorithmically; “subspace” means subset.
p04012.source: Thm. 1

p04013.statement: The canonical lift $L_m:=\varphi_m^{-1}\circ E_m:\mathcal X_m\to\mathcal Z$ satisfies $L_m\circ g_m=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal Z}$, and $L_m(x)$ is the unique $z$ with $E_m(x)=\varphi_m(z)$.
p04013.source: Cor. 1

p04014.statement: Cross-modal consistency: $\psi\circ L_m\circ g_m=\psi\circ L_n\circ g_n=\psi$ — observations of one latent state lift to one point — and $\iota_m(W_m)=\iota_n(W_n)=\psi(\mathcal Z)=\mathcal Z$.
p04014.source: Cor. 2

p04015.statement: Charts of the shell itself: for $\mathcal Z=\Fp$ the charts respecting the arithmetic are the frames $x\mapsto a+bx$ (1:C2), $\p(\p-1)$ of them, and $\Psi_{m\to n}$ between two frames is the one affine map carrying the first to the second (simply transitive) — the corpus’s coordinate systems are the paper’s charts.
p04015.source:
Section 3
master: 00:C1

p04016.statement: Foundational embeddings are adequate representations of one finite latent domain: cross-modal alignment, transferability and semantic coherence are the bijections $\Psi_{m\to n}$ (C1), consequences of the shared domain, not of architecture; the empirical record (A4) is their registered consequence. Falsifier: two adequate embeddings of one domain with no bijective translation on the resolved states.
p04016.source:
Section 4; Section 5.1; 00:A10
master: 00:A10

p04017.statement: Scope and limits: the theorem uses the finiteness of $\mathcal Z$ alone, no algebraic or geometric property of $\mathcal U_t$; the shell as host is the ontology’s claim (A3); optimisation decides when a representation is recovered, not which; non-stationary or weakly factorisable data may admit none; coordinate alignment may be intractable; nonlinearity as expansion and depth as shell complexity are analogies (Y1).
p04017.source: Section 1; Section 5; Interp. 2, 3

p04018.statement: The hypersphere [chart]: a Euclidean chart $\mathrm{Emb}:\mathcal Z\to\R^{d}$ equivariant for a symmetry acting transitively on $\mathcal Z$ and orthogonally on $\R^{d}$ has constant norm — $\mathrm{Emb}(\mathcal Z)\subset S^{d-1}$. The shell’s character chart $z\mapsto(\cos2\pi kz/\p,\sin2\pi kz/\p)_{k}$ is such a chart under translation, $\|\mathrm{Emb}(z)\|^{2}=\p-1$; in the shell’s arithmetic $\sum_{k}\g^{kz}\g^{k(n-z)}=n$ for every $z$.
p04018.source: Section 6

p04019.statement: Quantisation [chart]: a digital embedding has coordinates in a finite $\mathcal Q\subset\R$; at step $\Delta$ the distinguishable points on a sphere of radius $R$ number $N(R)\sim C_d(R/\Delta)^{d-1}$ (grid counts fit exponent $d-1$ at $d=2,3$); at fixed $d$, $\Delta$ the capacity grows with $R$.
p04019.source: Section 6.2; [Goldberg 1991; IEEE754Standard 2008; Conway & Sloane 1999]

p04020.statement: Gödel collapse: for distinct primes $p_1,\dots,p_d$ the code $G(x)=\prod p_i^{x_i}$ is injective on $\N^{d}$ (unique factorisation), and $G\bmod q$ stays injective on a finite set once $q$ exceeds its maximum; instance $d=3$, $x_i\le4$, primes $2,3,5$: $125$ codes, maximum $810\,000$, $q=810\,013$; signed coordinates are shifted first.
p04020.source: Section 6.3

p04021.statement: The reading of Section 6: the sphere is the continuous shadow of the shell — uniform radius the absence of intrinsic attributes, direction the relational content; the coordinate count is a representational artefact, every quantised vector one element of one field (E3); the radius reads the resolved domain’s size; Gödel codes establish representability only, not geometry or training.
p04021.source:
Section 6; 00:A10
master: 00:A10

p04025.statement: Learning objectives as approximations of adequacy (contrastive, masked prediction), algorithms for the projection maps $g_m$, and a general algebraic account of multimodal learning; named as future work (i), (ii), (iv), not claimed.

p04024.statement: Depth and the shell hierarchy: whether nonlinear layers correspond to innovation steps $\mathcal U_t\hookrightarrow\mathcal U_{t+1}$ and depth to arithmetic complexity (Interpretations 2, 3) as a theorem; named as future work (iii), not claimed.

p05001.statement: The classical theorems, accepted unchanged: Gödel I and Rosser, Tarski’s undefinability, Turing’s halting theorem, Cantor’s theorem and uncountability, Russell, Burali–Forti, Skolem, Vitali, Hausdorff, Banach–Tarski; the operational paradoxes (Hilbert’s hotel, Zeno). No classical derivation is disputed.
p05001.source: [G"odel 1931; Rosser 1936; Tarski 1956; Turing 1937; Cantor 1891; Russell 1903; Burali-Forti 1897; Skolem 1922; Vitali 1905; Hausdorff 1914; Banach & Tarski 1924]

p05002.statement: Metamathematics: Robinson’s $Q$, essentially undecidable, every model infinite; $\mathrm{Con}(Q)$ by cut elimination in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{superexp}$, not in $I\Delta_0+\mathrm{exp}$; Tait’s finitism; Dedekind’s categoricity of the second-order naturals; true second-order arithmetic not arithmetical; Tarski’s decidable real field; Solovay’s model and Shelah’s inaccessible.
p05002.source: [Tarski et al. 1953; H'ajek & Pudl'ak 1993; Wilkie & Paris 1987; Tait 1981; Shapiro 1991; Tarski 1951; Solovay 1970; Shelah 1984]

p05003.statement: Combinatorics and set theory: Fraenkel–Mostowski permutation models (symmetry as an obstruction to choice); de Bruijn–Erdős compactness of colouring; aperiodic tile sets and the undecidability of the domino problem (Berger, Robinson); Zermelo’s choice.
p05003.source: [Jech 1973; de Bruijn & ErdH os 1951; Berger 1966; Robinson 1971; Zermelo 1904]

p05004.statement: The corpus: the totality finite and complete (00:A4), counting closes by return (00:A7), a bounded observer a proper part and every reading a projection (00:A5, A6), Gödel vacuous over the finite $\Omega$ (00:Z1), the $\Omega$-hard demarcation (00:Z3); finite mathematics as ontologically primary (Lev, Zeilberger).
p05004.source: [Lev 2020; Zeilberger; Akhtman 2025]

p05005.statement: The standing hypotheses: (Eff) effective axiomatisation, (Arith) interpretability of $Q$, (Cns) consistency. Two doors for infinity: the meta-level syntax, potential and retained; and (IR), the object theory interprets $Q$ — an injective non-cyclic successor with sequence coding, the completed registry inside the theory.
p05005.source: Section 3; § 3.1

p05006.statement: The bundle $\{$Eff, Cns, Cmp, IR$\}$ is inconsistent, with no soundness assumption: under Eff and IR the Rosser sentence is available, and Cmp decides it against plain consistency.
p05006.source: Prop. 1; Thm. 3.3

p05007.statement: Witnessed independence: every three-element subset is satisfiable — $Q$ itself ($ eg$Cmp, consistent by finitary means, the superexponential cost exact); $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ ($ eg$IR: consistent, complete, decidable, singly axiomatised, interpreting no $Q$ since every model of $Q$ is infinite); the inconsistent extension ($ eg$Cns); true arithmetic ($ eg$Eff). Four legs, all load-bearing.
p05007.source:
Thm. 3.4
master: 00:A2

p05008.statement: The arithmetic frame $W_N$: domain $[0,N)$, constant $0$, order $<$, the graphs $S$, $A$, $M$ of successor, sum and product restricted to the domain (overflow fails the atom); frame truth is truth in $W_N$; a $\Delta_0$ sentence is transcribed through the graphs with guarded bounded quantifiers.
p05008.source: Def. 1; § 3.2

p05009.statement: Per-frame completeness: $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$ is consistent, complete and decidable, axiomatised by the categorical sentence $\sigma_N$; truth in any finite structure is decided by evaluation, and the theory of any structure is complete.
p05009.source: Prop. 2

p05010.statement: Bounded stability, schema form: a $\Delta_0$ sentence $\varphi$ with bound $t(\varphi)$ has $W_N\models\varphi^{*}\iff\N\models\varphi$ for every $N>t(\varphi)$, each instance $\mathrm{St}(\varphi,M)$ a finite conjunction of finite checks; proved for an explicit $\Delta_0$ language with $t(\varphi)$ computed; Goldbach below $20$ has $t=400$ and value true (below $10$, $t=100$, decided by the kernel).
p05010.source: Thm. 3.6; Ex. 3.7

p05011.statement: The unbounded quantifier is the internalised registry: a $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ sentence receives a verdict from each frame about its own domain and none about all frames at once; frame-relative completeness covers every executed verification (a bounded $\Delta_0$ trace) and no $\Pi^{0}_{1}$ closure.
p05011.source:
§ 3.2; D2; 00:Z3
master: 00:Z3

p05012.statement: The bounded agent of capacity $K$: records of at most $K$ symbols over $s\ge2$ letters, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ of them; certification is a retained record encoding a completed proof-check, one sentence per record, no schema compression.

p05013.statement: No internal mirror: fewer than $s^{K+1}$ records exist, so an agent with $s^{K+1}<N$ holds no injective representation of the domain of $W_N$ — a proper part cannot mirror the whole (pigeonhole).
p05013.source:
Prop. 3
master: 00:A5

p05014.statement: Vanishing certified fraction: at least $c^{L}$ normal-form sentences of length $\le L$, half of each cohort frame truths by completeness, fewer than $s^{K+1}$ certified, so the certified fraction is at most $s^{K+1}/\lfloor c^{L}/2\rfloor\to0$.
p05014.source: Prop. 4

p05015.statement: The migration: without IR every sentence about the totality is decided and incompleteness reappears as a resource bound on agents — the Gödel sentence’s role passes to truths whose shortest certificate exceeds the capacity; truth for $W_N$ is definable one level up (Tarski relativised to a resource hierarchy).
p05015.source:
§ 3.3; 00:Z1
master: 00:Z1

p05016.statement: Horizon separation: halting for machines of bounded space $K$ is decided from above within $|Q|\,K\,s^{K}$ steps (a configuration repeats) and never from within (diagonalisation); Turing’s theorem is an external non-existence theorem, classified with Cantor’s, not an instance of the bundle.
p05016.source: § 3.3

p05017.statement: The premises and baselines: AT (an absolute totality), IR (the internalised registry), AC$\infty$ (unrestricted choice over uncountable families); Cns, Cmp, Meas (the exact measure axioms of each geometry), and Det — a totality decides every well-posed question about itself, elements, subsets and relations, with its full second-order theory effectively presented; declared as an axiom.
p05017.source: § 4.1

p05018.statement: Antinomy normal form: Cns $+$ AT $+$ comprehension is inconsistent (Russell, Burali–Forti); the witness of Cns $+\neg$AT is bounded comprehension — every set $u$ has a subset not among its members and no universal set exists, decided on $V_4$.
p05018.source: Prop. 5

p05019.statement: Diagonal normal form: $\{$Eff, Cns, Cmp, IR$\}$ inconsistent (B2), Tarski a variant with the truth predicate for Cmp; the diagonal is a theorem when external — Cantor’s theorem, $n<2^{n}$ on every frame, uncountability, halting — and a paradox engine only over an internalised registry with completeness demanded.
p05019.source: Prop. 6; Rem. 4.1

p05020.statement: Choice normal forms: Vitali (countably additive translation-invariant measure on all subsets $+$ AC$\infty$ on $\R/\Q$, a countable amenable group) and Banach–Tarski (finitely additive isometry-invariant measure $+$ AC$\infty$ $+$ a free non-amenable rotation subgroup) are inconsistent bundles with distinct mechanisms; the finite witness is counting measure with definable choice.
p05020.source: Prop. 7

p05021.statement: The reductio principle: for each normal form a baseline $B$ and one infinitary premise $I$ with $B+I$ contradictory and $B+\neg I$ satisfiable by an explicit witness — bounded ranks, $\mathrm{Th}(W_N)$, counting measure (Solovay’s model as classical corroboration); the rejection of $I$ is coherent and witnessed.
p05021.source: Thm. 4.2; Table 1; B3, D2, D4

p05022.statement: The selection thesis: every normal form conjoins completed infinity with a totalising operation (comprehension, completeness, total selection, a total measure); each is harmless alone, contradiction tracks the conjunction; classical mathematics rejected the totalising conjunct at each crisis, this paper the shared one, the selection settled by Det rather than convention.
p05022.source: § 4.4; § 2.5

p05023.statement: Forced exit: Det supplies Eff and Cmp, so $\{$Cns, Det, IR$\}$ is inconsistent and, Cns and Det being constitutive, the reductio is forced against IR — no determinate totality internalises an unbounded registry; the four-clause bundle condenses to this triad. Conditional on Det.
p05023.source:
Prop. 8; B2
master: 00:A4

p05024.statement: Finiteness of determinate totalities: in ZF with every infinite set Dedekind-infinite, a structure satisfies Det iff it is finite — finite: the full higher-order theory decided by exhaustive evaluation; infinite: a copy of $\N$ inside gives an effective reduction of true second-order arithmetic, which is not arithmetical. The real field’s first-order tameness is silence about its subsets.
p05024.source:
Prop. 9
master: 00:A4

p05025.statement: Corollaries: no absolute totality is determinate (a universal set is infinite by the iterated singletons); Meas is decided content — a Det totality decides every measure question, trivially on a finite one (counting measure). The totalising conjuncts of two normal forms follow from D8.
p05025.source: Cor. 1; Cor. 2

p05026.statement: The three gates: syntactic infinity (meta-level, potential, retained), semantic infinity (a completed object of the theory, the target in all three forms), diagonalisation (a method, dangerous only downstream of the second gate); the paper argues with an unbounded supply of finite objects only.
p05026.source: § 4.5; Table 2

p05027.statement: Global choice on a finite universe: with a canonical order, $\operatorname{ch}(A)=\min A$ is a uniform pointwise choice rule; over a fixed finite base AC is a definable theorem; finite products are nonempty without it.
p05027.source: Prop. 10

p05028.statement: Periodic choice: an equality-periodic family $A_{i+N}=A_i$ has the choice $f(i)=\operatorname{ch}(A_i)$ of the same period; group-periodic families as equivariant surjections $\pi:A\to I$ with equivariant sections.
p05028.source: Lemma 5.2; Def. 5

p05029.statement: Equivariant periodic choice: a $G$-equivariant section exists iff each stabiliser action $G_i\curvearrowright A_i$ has a fixed point (one orbit at a time); the Fraenkel–Mostowski mechanism in positive form.
p05029.source: Thm. 5.3

p05030.statement: The definable basis: every subspace of a finite vector space has the greedy $\min$-basis, one definable function on all subspaces; the equivariant obstruction — $\Z/2$ acting by $v\mapsto-v$ on the line over $\F_5$ fixes no basis ($-v\neq v$), over $\F_2$ it does: arithmetic, not formal.
p05030.source: Thm. 5.4; Ex. 5.5

p05031.statement: Periodic Kőnig: in a finite digraph with out-degree $\ge1$ the greedy walk repeats a vertex within $|D|+1$ steps and is eventually periodic with period $\le|D|$ — the pigeonhole on an iteration over finitely many states.
p05031.source: Lemma 5.6

p05032.statement: Periodic de Bruijn–Erdős, dimension one: a $\sigma$-periodic graph of bounded range whose finite subgraphs are $c$-colourable admits a definable $\sigma^{m}$-periodic $c$-colouring (the transfer digraph $D_c$, its sub-digraph of vertices beginning walks of every length, E5).
p05032.source: Thm. 5.7

p05033.statement: The dimension boundary: in $\Z^{2}$ aperiodic tile sets exist — every finite patch admissible, no periodic configuration — and the domino problem is undecidable; the passage from finite admissibility to infinite realisability has no finite certificate, its demarcation none either. The finite reading asserts patch admissibility only.
p05033.source: § 5.4; A3

p05034.statement: The choice paradoxes vanish: on a finite set counting measure is complete and invariant, no decomposition doubles the set ($X\sqcup X$ does not inject into $X$), and every ultrafilter is principal; periodic variants inherit this on one period.
p05034.source: § 5.5

p05035.statement: Ontology and conservativeness: actual infinity is an idealisation of the finite; the bounded fragment is kept exactly, the unbounded fragment in schema form; analysis as approximation over finite grids; choice in the small. Positioning: finitism, intuitionism, ultrafinitism, structuralism; the potential-infinity rule retained at the meta-level as a commitment, not a neutrality.
p05035.source:
§ 6; § 6; § 6.1; 00:A2
master: 00:A2

p05036.statement: The Reductio Rule and its two tribunals: the economic ledger (the classical exit keeps $\Pi_1$, $\Pi_2$ number theory at a superexponential consistency grant; the finite exit keeps the bounded fragment and declines one classically provable existence claim, E7) and the constitutive Det, on which the verdict rests; objections O1–O5 answered.
p05036.source: § 6.2; § 6.3

p05037.statement: The catalogue: the pathologies of the completed infinite in four classes — antinomies, consistent-but-unregistrable, underdetermination, physical divergences — each removed by finiteness; the one exclusion retained, the schema over finite instances and the successor act.
p05037.source: Appendix A

p05041.statement: The standing of the iteration rule — whether the potential-infinity rule of the meta-level can be rejected, and at what cost — is the subject of companion work; the present results are stated to survive either outcome.
p05041.source: § 6.1

p06001.statement: The framed substrate: the Subject $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$ with $\p=4\kap+1$, its register $\pi=2\kap$, $\im=-\gen^{\kap}=\gen^{-\kap}$, $e=\gen^{\im}$; the frame-relative labels and the atlas of presentations $\gen\mapsto\gen^{u}$; time as scale-dilation, the generator as the observer’s own advance.
p06001.source: [Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2026; Akhtman 2025]

p06002.statement: The Weil representation $\omega_\p$ of $\SL(2,\Fp)$ and its Schrödinger model, the finite Fourier transform representing the rotation $w$, the finite harmonic oscillator; the scalar convention $\omega_\p(w)^{2}=\omega_\p(-I)$, $\omega_\p(w)^{4}=I$.
p06002.source: [Weil 1964; Gurevich & Hadani 2006; Gurevich et al. 2008]

p06003.statement: The classical evaluation of the twisted quadratic Gauss sum for $4\mid n$, $\sum_k\zeta_n^{uk^{2}}=\bigl(\tfrac{\kap}{u}\bigr)(1\pm i)\sqrt n$; the eigenvalue quartet of prime-modulus number-theoretic transforms; the multiplicity counts of the discrete Fourier eigenvalues.
p06003.source: [Berndt et al. 1998; Birtwistle 1982; McClellan & Parks 1972]

p06004.statement: The entropic uncertainty relation for a pair of bases, $H_{B}+H_{B'}\ge-2\log c$, $c$ the maximal overlap, $c=n^{-1/2}$ for mutually unbiased bases, saturated by basis-localized states.
p06004.source: [Hirschman 1957; Bialynicki-Birula & Mycielski 1975; Maassen & Uffink 1988; Wehner & Winter 2010]

p06005.statement: The framed-rational zoom: the grids $G_n$ and their $(\p-1)$-periodicity $G_{n+(\p-1)}=G_n$, the meridian shift $m\mapsto m-1$ as the refinement step.
p06005.source: [Akhtman 2025, §4.3, Lemma 2]

p06006.statement: The measurement layer: probabilities are structural weights of the cyclotomic stratum, the finite-field module carries no Born magnitude, and the readout is an observer-side declaration; the shell dynamics a bijection, entropy attaching to the readout.
p06006.source: [Akhtman & Voether 2026; Akhtman 2025]

p06007.statement: The continuum fractional Fourier transform and the finite constructions the family is separated from: the eigenbasis and matrix-function transforms, the harmonic-oscillator propagator reading.
p06007.source: [Namias 1980; Ozaktas et al. 2001; Lima & Campello de Souza 2012; Pei et al. 2011; Lima et al. 2017]

p06008.statement: Shell data, capacity-first: $\kap$ primary, $\p=4\kap+1$, the meridian cycle $\Phit=\Z_{4\kap}$, the oriented quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$ (clockwise phase convention), $\pi=2\kap$, $e=\gen^{\im}$; the meridians $M_s=\{a\gen^{s}:a\in I_\p\}$; the six shells of Table 1 with their generators and quarter-turns.
p06008.source: § 3, (3.1), (3.2)

p06009.statement: The Euler identity is a property of the chart class: $e^{\im\pi}=\gen^{2\kap(\im\bmod2)}\equiv-1$ exactly when the quarter-turn residue is odd; the conjugate reframing $(\gen,\im)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-\im)$ toggles the parity, so one member of each conjugate pair carries it; on $\F_{13}(\chron;0,1,2)$, $\im=5$ and $6^{6}=-1$. Every primitive frame of the six shells.
p06009.source:
§ 3
master: 00:C14

p06010.statement: Chart covariance: under $\gen'=\gen^{u}$, $u\in\Zp^{\times}$, the quarter-turn name flips exactly on $u\equiv3\pmod4$ and the exponential-unit name moves already at $u\equiv1\pmod4$ whenever $\im(u-1)\not\equiv0\pmod{4\kap}$ ($\p=13$, $u=5$: $e'=2\neq6$); the registered objects (C3, C4, C9, F3) are invariant.
p06010.source: Rem. 3.2

p06011.statement: The shell Fourier matrix $\Wt_{kj}=\gen^{jk}$ on $\Vt=\Fp^{\Phit}$, the reversal $J$, the normalized shell Fourier operator $\Ft=\im\Wt$.
p06011.source: (4.2), (4.1), (4.3)

p06012.statement: $\Wt^{2}=-J$, $\Ft^{2}=J$, $\Ft^{4}=I$: the normalized operator generates the four-cycle, on the six shells of Table 1.
p06012.source:
Lem. 4.2, Prop. 4.5
master: 00:C2

p06013.statement: The normalization is the unitary constant read in the field: $1/n\equiv-1$, its square roots in $\Fp$ are exactly $\pm\im$, and $(c\Wt)^{2}=J$ if and only if $c=\pm\im$.
p06013.source: Rem. 4.4

p06014.statement: $\Wt J=J\Wt$, hence $\Ft J=J\Ft$; $\Vt=V^{+}\oplus V^{-}$ with $\dim V^{+}=2\kap+1$, $\dim V^{-}=2\kap-1$.
p06014.source: Lem. 5.5

p06015.statement: The projectors $\Pi_\ell=\tfrac14\sum_{r=0}^{3}\im^{-\ell r}\Ft^{r}$ and the principal framed character lift $\Ft^{[s]}=\sum_\ell\gen^{-\ell s}\Pi_\ell$, $s\in\Phit$: the refinement base is the inverse generator, $(\gen^{-1})^{\kap}=\im$, each projector’s character the $\ell$-th power of the meridian phase $z_s=\gen^{-s}$.
p06015.source: (5.2), (5.3), Rem. 5.3

p06016.source: Lem. 5.1

p06017.statement: The exact finite-field FrFT: $s\mapsto\Ft^{[s]}$ is a representation of $\Phit$, $\Ft^{[s+r]}=\Ft^{[s]}\Ft^{[r]}$ on every pair of the six shells, with the cardinal values $\Ft^{[0]}=I$, $\Ft^{[\kap]}=\Ft$, $\Ft^{[2\kap]}=J$, $\Ft^{[3\kap]}=\Ft^{-1}$, and $(\Ft^{[1]})^{\kap}=\Ft$.
p06017.source:
Thm. 5.4
master: 00:C2

p06018.statement: Faithfulness: $s\mapsto\Ft^{[s]}$ is injective on $\Z_{4\kap}$ for every $\kap\ge1$; at $\p=5$ the surviving odd projector carries the faithful character.
p06018.source: Thm. 5.9

p06019.statement: The multiplicities $m_\ell=\operatorname{rank}\Pi_\ell=\dim\ker(\Ft-\im^{\ell}I)$: $m_0+m_2=2\kap+1$, $m_1+m_3=2\kap-1$; $m_0,m_2\ge1$; $m_1,m_3\ge1$ for $\kap\ge2$; at $\p=5$ exactly one of $\Pi_1,\Pi_3$ vanishes.
p06019.source: Lem. 5.6

p06020.statement: Multiplicities are chart data: the vertex relabelling $m\mapsto um$ carries $\Ft(\gen)$ to $\Ft(\gen^{u^{2}})$ by a coordinate permutation; at $\p=13$ the frames $\gen=2$ and $\gen=6$ give $(3,3,4,2)$ and $(4,2,3,3)$, traces $4$ and $9$.
p06020.source: Rem. 5.7

p06021.statement: The multiplicity dichotomy: with $G=\sum_{k}\gen^{k^{2}}=\varepsilon(1+\im)$ (A3), the tuple is $(\kap,\kap,\kap+1,\kap-1)$ for $\varepsilon=+1$ and $(\kap+1,\kap-1,\kap,\kap)$ for $\varepsilon=-1$; $GG^{*}=-2$ and $\varepsilon(\gen^{-1})=-\varepsilon(\gen)$. Exact on the $38$ primitive frames of $\p\in\{5,13,17,29,37\}$ and the $16$ of $\p=41$.
p06021.source: Thm. 5.8

p06022.statement: Exponent lifts: every lift $a_\ell\equiv\ell\pmod4$, $U^{(a)}_s=\sum_\ell\gen^{-a_\ell s}\Pi_\ell$, is additive with the same cardinal skeleton, $U^{(a)}_{s+r}=U^{(a)}_sU^{(a)}_r$ and $U^{(a)}_{m\kap}=\Ft^{m}$.
p06022.source: Rem. 5.3

p06023.statement: The conjugate reframing $(\gen,\im)\mapsto(\gen^{-1},-\im)$: exactly $\Ft'=-\Ft^{-1}$ and $\Pi'_\ell=\Pi_{\ell+2}$; the operator relations, cardinal values, additivity and faithfulness hold on the conjugate frame, and its multiplicity tuple is the other pattern of C7.
p06023.source:
Rem. 3.2, Thm. 5.8
master: 00:C7

p06051.statement: The sign under chart change: $\varepsilon(\gen^{u})=\bigl(\tfrac{\kap}{u}\bigr)\varepsilon(\gen)$ for $u\equiv1\pmod4$, the two classes equally populated on every shell of Table 1; the identities $G^{2}=2\im$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft=\im G$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft^{2}=2$, $\operatorname{Tr}\Ft^{3}=\im G^{*}$ of the proof of C7.
p06051.source: Thm. 5.8

p06052.statement: Charts outside the classified set: a family canonical in the chart $\gen^{u}$ with $u^{2}\not\equiv1\pmod{4\kap}$ does not commute with $\Ft$ — $\p=29$, $u=5$, and every such chart of the six shells of Table 1.
p06052.source: Rem. 5.3

p06024.statement: The meridional representation domain $D_s=(\Vt,\mathcal B_s)$, $\mathcal B_s=\Ft^{[s]}\mathcal B_0$, every $\Ft^{[s]}$ invertible; the cardinal domains spatial, spectral, parity, inverse-spectral.
p06024.source: Def. 6.1, Cor. 6.2

p06025.statement: The $4\kap$ framed domains are pairwise distinct; read as unordered measurement bases $B_{s+2\kap}=B_s$, since $\Ft^{[s+2\kap]}=\Ft^{[s]}J$ and $J$ permutes the standard basis.
p06025.source: Cor. 6.3, Rem. 6.4

p06026.statement: The meridian-step interval $I_\p=\{0,1,\dots,\pi\}$, the meridian-scale map $S_r(x)=\gen^{r}x$, and the local scale chart $\gen\mapsto\lambda>1$ reading the effective step $\gen^{m}$ as $\lambda^{m}$ [chart].
p06026.source: (7.1), Def. 7.1, Def. 7.5

p06027.statement: Meridian-scale covariance: $S_r(M_m)=M_{m+r}$ for every $(m,r)$, as ordered lists; consecutive entries of $M_m$ differ by the effective step $\gen^{m}$; $S_{r+(\p-1)}=S_r$, the periodicity of A5 in meridian form.
p06027.source:
Prop. 7.2, Cor. 7.4, Rem. 7.3
master: 00:C2

p06028.statement: Meridian zoom [chart]: $M_m$ reads the meridian-coordinate vector at step $\lambda^{\tilde m}$, the forward shift zoom-out and the inverse shift zoom-in, the seam an aliasing return; at $\p=13$, $\gen=2$ the ladder $M_0,\dots,M_3$ at steps $1,2,4,8$, unwrapped within $w\gen^{r}<\p$ ($w=\pi=6$: $r\le1$) and wrapping from $M_2$.
p06028.source: Thm. 7.6, Ex. 7.8, Rem. 7.9

p06029.statement: Scope of the unification: the representation-side rotation and the coordinate-side scale shift act on carriers of different dimension and are not equal as operators; they share the index group $\Phit$ and the cardinal labels, and the operator-level relation is E5–E7.
p06029.source: Rem. 7.9

p06053.statement: The cycle carries exactly $2\kap$ measurement bases: $B_{s+t} eq B_s$ for $t otin\{0,2\kap\}$, since every off-site entry of row $0$ of $\Ft^{[t]}$ is $ frac{\im}{2}(1-\gen^{-2t}) eq0$ and $\Ft^{[t]}$ is not monomial; the six shells of Table 1.
p06053.source: Rem. 6.4

p06030.statement: The Weil-side data: $z_s=\gen^{-s}$, $c_s=(z_s+z_s^{-1})/2$, $d_s=(z_s-z_s^{-1})/(2\im)$, the rotation $R_s$; the pulled-back family $\operatorname{FrFT}^{\rm Weil}_\kap(s)=\omega_\p(R_s)$; cardinal Weil correspondence of two families.
p06030.source: (8.1)–(8.3), (8.5), Def. 8.4

p06031.statement: $R_s\in SO(2,\Fp)$, and $s\mapsto R_s$ is an isomorphism $\Phit\simeq SO(2,\Fp)$ with $|SO(2,\Fp)|=\p-1=4\kap$: the full rotation group of the $\p^{2}$-point plane is the meridian cycle.
p06031.source: Lem. 8.1, Prop. 8.2

p06032.statement: The cardinal-skeleton dictionary $M_s\leftrightarrow s\leftrightarrow z_s\leftrightarrow R_s$ with $R_0=I$, $R_\kap=w$, $R_{2\kap}=-I$, $R_{3\kap}=w^{-1}$ (the $R_\kap$ column of Table 1), $z_\kap=\im$; the FRC-native and Weil families stand in cardinal Weil correspondence, the Weil side by the normalization of A2.
p06032.source: Thm. 8.5

p06033.statement: Scope and reading of the dictionary: agreement on the four cardinal indices only, the two families acting on spaces of different dimension over different coefficient rings; the holographic reading, the rotation symmetry of the $\p^{2}$-point plane carried by a cycle of the size of its square root, the state side of dimension $\p$.
p06033.source: Rem. 8.6, Rem. 8.7

p06034.statement: Spectral obstruction: for $\kap\ge2$ no invertible $T$ on $\Vt$ satisfies $T\sigma T^{-1}=\Ft^{[s]}$ for any $s$; the cyclic groups $\langle\sigma\rangle$ and $\langle\Ft^{[1]}\rangle$, of the same order $4\kap$, are not conjugate.
p06034.source: Prop. 8.8

p06035.statement: Common character sector: on $E_1=\operatorname{im}\Pi_1\neq0$ ($\kap\ge2$) $\Ft^{[s]}=\gen^{-s}I$, the intertwiner $\Ft^{[s]}T_v=T_vS_{-s}$ on every $x\in\Fp$ and $s$, and $R_s(1,-\im)^{\mathsf T}=\gen^{-s}(1,-\im)^{\mathsf T}$.
p06035.source: Prop. 8.9

p06036.statement: Cardinal Heisenberg covariance: $\Ft\sigma\Ft^{-1}=D_1$, $\Ft D_1\Ft^{-1}=\sigma^{-1}$; $\Ft^{r}\sigma=\sigma_r\Ft^{r}$ with $(\sigma,D_1,\sigma^{-1},D_1^{-1})$; the expansion (8.7); $\Ft^{[s]}\sigma\Ft^{[s]-1}$ monomial exactly at the four cardinal indices and non-monomial at every one of the $112$ intermediate indices of $\p\in\{13,17,29,37,41\}$.
p06036.source: Prop. 8.10, § 8.1

p06050.statement: Cardinal exclusivity: for every $s\notin\{0,\kap,2\kap,3\kap\}$ the operator (8.7) is not monomial — off $j\in\{-1,0,1\}$ its row $0$ is $x^{-1}$ times a quadratic in $x=\gen^{j}$ with leading coefficient $\im\,[c_0(s)+c_2(s)]\,c_3(-s)\neq0$, $c_0(s)+c_2(s)=\tfrac12(1+\gen^{-2s})$, so the row has at least $4\kap-5$ nonzero entries; the count checked on every shell below $200$.
p06050.source: Thm. 8.11

p06054.statement: The spectra behind E5: $\sigma$ is diagonalizable over $\Fp$ with the $4\kap$ simple eigenvalues $\Fpx$; $\Ft^{[s]}=\sum_\ell\gen^{-\ell s}\Pi_\ell$ has at most four, among the $\gen^{-\ell s}$ ($\Ft^{[1]}$ on the six shells).
p06054.source: Prop. 8.8

p06037.statement: The readout algebra $A=\Z[\tfrac{1}{4n},X,Y,Y^{-1}]/(\Phi_n(X),Y^{2}-n)$ with the continuum chart $\sigma_\C$ ($X\mapsto\zeta_n$, $Y\mapsto+\sqrt n$) and the framed reduction $\rho$ ($X\mapsto\gen$, $Y\mapsto-\im$); the readout of a shell state as the Born vector of a selected lift, its Shannon entropy in nats, not thermodynamic.

p06038.statement: $\widehat G^{2}=2n\,X^{\kap}$ in $A$, exact modulo $\Phi_n(X)$; under $\sigma_\C$, $(\sum_k\zeta_n^{k^{2}})^{2}=2n\,i$; under $\rho$, $G^{2}=2\im$, the reduction the proof of C7 uses.
p06038.source: Def. 9.1, Thm. 5.8

p06039.statement: Entropic cardinal values $H(0)=H(2\kap)=0$, $H(\kap)=H(3\kap)=\log n$ for every site-localized input; $B_0$ and $B_\kap$ mutually unbiased, $H_{B_0}+H_{B_\kap}\ge\log n$ saturated by the localized states and by the comb $(\delta_0+\delta_6)/\sqrt2$ at $n=12$, $\log2+\log6=\log12$ [approx].
p06039.source: Prop. 9.2

p06040.statement: The closed form for $\delta_0$: $p_0=1-\tfrac{n-1}{n}t_s$, $p_{j\neq0}=t_s/n$, $t_s=(2-\zeta_n^{2s}-\zeta_n^{-2s})/4$, read as $\sin^{2}(\pi s/2\kap)$; $H(s)$ strictly increasing on $[0,\kap]$, two oscillations per cycle, strictly intermediate off the cardinal indices [approx].
p06040.source: Prop. 9.3

p06041.statement: $\p=13$: $H(s)/\log n=0,\,.44,\,.91,\,1,\,.91,\,.44$ over each half-cycle; Figure 2 regenerated [approx].
p06041.source: § 9.1

p06042.statement: Input dependence: $\delta_1$ gives $H(1)/\log n=0.55$ against $0.44$ for $\delta_0$; $\delta_j$ meets the odd projectors exactly for $j\notin\{0,2\kap\}$, and $\delta_{2\kap}$ reproduces the $\delta_0$ curve [approx].
p06042.source: Rem. 9.4

p06043.statement: The Galois twist $X\mapsto\zeta_n^{u}$ leaves the cardinal values of every $\delta_j$ invariant and relabels the curve of $\delta_j$ by $s\mapsto us$ whenever $\eta uj\equiv j\pmod n$ ($\eta u\equiv1\pmod4$): at every cardinal site, and at every site for $u=-1$; off the cardinal sites $u\not\equiv\pm1$ can change the curve ($n=12$, $u=5$, $s=1$: $\delta_1$ $0.55\mapsto0.44$, $\delta_3$ $0.42$ unchanged) [approx].
p06043.source: Prop. 9.5

p08001.statement: The framed substrate: the symmetry-complete shell $\p=4\kap+1$ with frame $\Fp(t;0,1,g)$, the derived quarter-turn $\im=g^{-\kap}$, $\pi=2\kap$, $e=g^{\im}$, the residue web with $c^{2}=2^{-1}$; the orbital shell with its meridians $M_m$ and latitude circles $L_a$; the relational stance under which the continuum is a projection.
p08001.source: [Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2026; Akhtman 2025]

p08002.statement: Finite-field algebra: the quadratic extension $K=\Fp[\w]/(\w^{2}-\nu)$ with Frobenius conjugation and norm, Hilbert’s Theorem 90, the square classes by Euler’s criterion, the unitary group of a nondegenerate Hermitian form over a finite field.
p08002.source: [Lidl & Niederreiter 1997; Lam 2005; Taylor 1992]

p08003.statement: The continuum antecedents: the Cayley transform and the Crank–Nicolson step, Clifford algebras and the Dirac matrices, the $1{+}1$ Lorentz boost and its spin lift, the Schwinger unitary basis and the finite-field quantum mechanics it is compared with.
p08003.source: [Crank & Nicolson 1947; Chevalley 1996; Porteous 1995; Schwinger 1960; Chang et al. 2013; Chang et al. 2013; Lev 2010]

p08004.statement: The Hartley (max-)entropy reading of image counts, and reversibility as zero information loss.
p08004.source: [Hartley 1928; R'enyi 1961; Landauer 1961; Bennett 1973; Fredkin & Toffoli 1982]

p08005.statement: The programme’s admissibility congruences ($\kap$ even, $\kap\equiv1\pmod3$, $\p\equiv5\pmod{12}$), the laboratory Carrier $\Omega=2\,408\,561$ with $S=602\,140$, and the constants web ($c^{2}=2^{-1}$, $\hbar=\im$).
p08005.source: [Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2026]

p08006.statement: The programme position: the primary object a finite symmetry space of algebraic possibilities, every description an incomplete projection; the theorems of the paper stand independently of it.
p08006.source: [Akhtman 2025], § 7

p08007.statement: The shells in play: the worked Subject shells $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$, the coordinate shell $Y=\Fp^{4}$, the coefficient field $K$; the two conjugation registers — $\im\in\Fp$ Frobenius-fixed, the internal Euclidean phase, and $\w$ the conjugation of the extension; Carrier-scale statements are transfer targets, never sites of computation.
p08007.source: Rems. 2, 3

p08008.statement: The class is the datum: $\Fpx/(\Fpx)^{2}$ has order two, any two nonsquares differ by a square factor, and the Lorentzian form depends on $\nu$ only through its class.
p08008.source: Lem. 1

p08009.statement: The drive is canonical: $g$ is a nonsquare on every shell and the only named residue whose class is nonsquare on every symmetry-complete shell; $\im$, $2$, $2^{-1}$, $-2$ are squares exactly when $\kap$ is even; $e=g^{\im}$ has no stable class; $[g^{-1}]=[g]$. Exhaustive on $\p<2000$.
p08009.source: Lem. 2

p08010.statement: The two speed-of-light seats: $\nu=g=c^{2}\cdot(2g)$ exactly on every shell; $[c^{2}]$ is even iff $\kap$ is even, $[2g]$ odd iff $\kap$ is even, the product odd always; the temporal coefficient is not $c^{2}$; anchors $\F_{13}$ ($2^{-1}=7$ nonsquare), $\F_{17}$ ($2,\im,e$ squares), and the laboratory Carrier ($c=171\,106$ base-rational, $1\,204\,281\cdot12=6=g$).
p08010.source:
Rem. 4, Cor. 1
master: 00:C3

p08011.statement: The square class is chronon parity: the squares are $\langle g^{2}\rangle$, a residue’s class is the parity of its drive-step count; on $\kap$-even shells every element of $Q_4=\{1,\im,-1,-\im\}$ is a square, so the order-four chart grading carries no signature. Exhaustive over every primitive root of $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$; Euler form on $\p<2000$.
p08011.source:
Thm. 1
master: 00:C8, 00:B10

p08012.statement: Norm growth and parity: $N(gz)=g^{2}N(z)$ with $g^{2}$ a square, the single-chronon multiplier $g$ odd, $x^{2}=\nu$ unsolvable in $\Fp$; the flip $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ preserves the parity class.
p08012.source:
Thm. 2
master: 00:C8

p08013.statement: Signature lives on $\Fp$: the Euclidean form has $\p^{3}+\p^{2}-\p$ zeros (hyperbolic, Witt index two), $Q_\nu$ has $\p^{3}-\p^{2}+\p$ (elliptic, Witt index one) on every symmetry-complete $\p<60$; $2353$ and $2041$ at $\p=13$; over $K$ every element of $\Fp$ is a square and the dichotomy collapses.
p08013.source: Rem. 5

p08014.statement: One-way and two-way transport: comparison (two-way) readings are even-parity, the one-way single-chronon multiplier odd, and the null-cone slope $\sqrt\nu=g^{1/2}$ is no base-field ratio — light-like transport carries no registered velocity, only its square class. Falsifier: a registered one-way velocity, or a two-way constant that changes under the synchronisation gauge $g\mapsto g^{-1}$ (B6).
p08014.source: Rem. 6; Thm. 2

p08015.statement: The Hermitian form $\langle\psi,\phi\rangle_X=\sum\overline{\psi(x)}\phi(x)$ on $\calH(X)$, the adjoint, the finite unitary group; the Euclidean configuration space $X_d=\Fp^{d}$ with translations $T_u$, forward and backward differences and the Laplacian $\Delta_E$; the Hamiltonian $H_{E,V,\vkap}=-\vkap\Delta_E+M_V$ with the stiffness $\vkap$ distinct from the capacity $\kap$.
p08015.source: Defs. 1, 2, 3, 4

p08016.statement: The form is Hermitian and nondegenerate; $T_u$ is unitary with $T_u^{\dagger}=T_{-u}$; $\Delta_E$ and $H_{E,V,\vkap}$ are self-adjoint; under $A\in\mathrm{GL}_d(\Fp)$ the pullback $A_*$ intertwines translations, differences and Laplacians of the two frames.
p08016.source: Lem. 3, Props. 1, 2, Cor. 2, Lem. 4

p08017.statement: The Cayley step $U_{\alpha,H}=(I-\alpha H)^{-1}(I+\alpha H)$ for $\alpha\in K^{-}$ (the recursion $(I-\alpha H)\psi_{n+1}=(I+\alpha H)\psi_n$); the admissible set $\calA(H)=\{\alpha\in K^{-}:\det(I-\alpha H)\ne0\}$.
p08017.source: Defs. 5, 6, Rem. 10

p08018.statement: Exact Hermitian preservation: for self-adjoint $H$ and admissible $\alpha$ the Cayley step is unitary, and every orbit is periodic.
p08018.source: Thm. 3, Cor. 3

p08019.statement: The finite Cayley transform: $\varphi(\lambda)=(1+\alpha\lambda)/(1-\alpha\lambda)$ is defined on all of $\Fp$, takes values in the norm-one torus $N^{1}$, and with $\varphi(\infty)=-1$ bijects $\mathbb P^{1}(\Fp)$ onto $N^{1}$, $|N^{1}|=\p+1$; the unitary group of one channel is $N^{1}$; the orientation gauge $\alpha\mapsto-\alpha$ inverts every $\varphi(\lambda)$ and imports the derived orientation of the shell.
p08019.source: Thm. 4, Rem. 11

p08020.statement: The $\F_{13}$ Schrödinger example: $H=-\Delta_E$ on $\F_{13}$ is nilpotent, so $\calA(H)=K^{-}$; at $\alpha=c$, $U^{13}=I$; every $\alpha=kc$, $k\ne0$, gives order $13$, and $U$ is unitary for the form.
p08020.source: Ex. 1

p08021.statement: Spinor fields $\calS(Y)=K^{4}$-valued on the coordinate shell, the forward differences $ abla_\mu$, the gamma matrices (5.2) with $\eta=\diag(- u,1,1,1)$, the standard finite Dirac operator $\mathcal D_{E_0}=\sum_\mu\gamma^{\mu} abla_\mu$ and the finite Dirac equation $(\mathcal D_{E_0}-m)\psi=0$.
p08021.source: (5.2), Def. 7

p08022.source: Prop. 3

p08024.statement: The $1{+}1$ boost $\Lambda(x,y)$ with entries $A,B$ from $x^{2}-\nu y^{2}=\delta\ne0$; the spin lift $S(x,y)=xI_4+y\gamma^{0}\gamma^{1}$; the spinor transport $\mathcal T_{\Lambda,S}=S\Lambda_*$ and the transported operator $\mathcal D_{\Lambda,S}$.
p08024.source: Def. 8, (5.19)

p08025.statement: The boost group is the non-split torus: $\Lambda(x,y)\in O(Q_ u,\Fp)$, $G_ u$ a subgroup, $z\mapsto\Lambda$ a surjection $K^{ imes} o G_ u$ with kernel $\Fpx$ and $A-B\w=z/ ar z$; $G_ u\simeq N^{1}\simeq C_{\p+1}$, cyclic; an order-three boost exists iff $3\mid\p+1$ ($|G_3|=18$ at $17$, $|G_2|=14$ at $13$).
p08025.source: Props. 5, 6, Lem. 5

p08026.source: Prop. 4

p08027.statement: The transported family: $ abla^{E_\Lambda}_\mu\Lambda_*=\Lambda_* abla^{E_0}_\mu$; $\mathcal D_{\Lambda,S}=\sum\widehat\gamma^{\mu} abla^{E_\Lambda}_\mu$ with $\widehat\gamma^{0}=A\gamma^{0}- u B\gamma^{1}$, $\widehat\gamma^{1}=-B\gamma^{0}+A\gamma^{1}$; the transported Clifford relations and factorization.
p08027.source: Lem. 6, Prop. 7, Cor. 4, Thm. 6

p08028.statement: Exact covariance: $\mathcal D_{\Lambda,S}\mathcal T_{\Lambda,S}\psi=\mathcal T_{\Lambda,S}\mathcal D_{E_0}\psi$, solutions transported to solutions; verified on a sample field at $\p=13$.
p08028.source: Cor. 5

p08029.statement: The spinor form: under the plain conjugate transpose the gammas carry mixed signs ($\gamma^{2}$ the obstruction) and the $\gamma^{0}$-twist fails; $X=\gamma^{0}\gamma^{1}\gamma^{3}$ is Hermitian with $X^{2}=\nu$, commutes with $\gamma^{0},\gamma^{1},\gamma^{3}$, anticommutes with $\gamma^{2}$, and $X^{-1}(\gamma^{\mu})^{\dagger}X=-\gamma^{\mu}$ for all $\mu$; $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_X$ is nondegenerate Hermitian, $T-T^{-1}$ nilpotent and anti-self-adjoint, $\mathcal D^{s}$ $X$-self-adjoint and nilpotent ($\p=5,13,17$).
p08029.source: Lem. 7

p08030.statement: Exact Dirac evolution: the Cayley step of $H=\mathcal D^{s}-mI$ preserves $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_X$; for $m=0$ admissibility is automatic, $U$ unipotent with order a power of $\p$ ($25=\p^{2}$ in the $1{+}1$ computation at $\p=5$); for $m\ne0$, $U=\varphi(-m)V$ and $\operatorname{ord}(U)=\operatorname{lcm}(\p^{a},\operatorname{ord}_{N^{1}}\varphi(-m))$ ($75$, $150$ at $m=1,2$).
p08030.source: Thm. 7

p08031.statement: The two Dirac operators are one covariant family: the pullback identity holds for the symmetric differences, $\mathcal T_{\Lambda,S}$ carries $\mathcal D^{s}$ to its transported form, and the spinor form transports by the norm, $S(x,y)^{\#}=S(x,-y)=\delta S^{-1}$: norm-one lifts preserve $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle_X$ exactly, the odd coset scales it by the nonsquare class.
p08031.source: Prop. 8

p08032.statement: The worked shells: $\F_{13}$ with $\nu=g=2$, $x=y=1$: $A=10$, $B=2$, $S=I+\gamma^{0}\gamma^{1}$, $\widehat\gamma^{0}=10\gamma^{0}-4\gamma^{1}$, $\widehat\gamma^{1}=-2\gamma^{0}+10\gamma^{1}$; $\F_{17}$ the minimal admissible shell ($17\equiv5\bmod12$, no smaller symmetry-complete prime), $\im=4$, $2,\im,e$ squares, $\nu=3$, $A=15$, $B=1$, $|G_3|=18$, triality present.
p08032.source: Exs. 2, 3

p08033.statement: Mass is winding rate: the finite Dirac equation equates the meridional development rate of the spinor field to $m$ times the field, the finite seat of the energy–momentum–mass relation, $E=hf$ an identity. Falsifier: that of the corpus row it instantiates — a rest mass with no cycle winding, or a stationary state whose registered frequency is not its winding index.
p08033.source: Rem. 12

p08034.statement: The image count $I_X(f)=|f(X)|$ and the loss factor $L_X(f)=|X|/|f(X)|$; the Hartley reading, a map losing exactly $\log L_X(f)$ of distinguishability.
p08034.source: Def. 9, Rem. 13

p08035.statement: A self-map is bijective iff $L_X(f)=1$; the power map $x\mapsto x^{\varepsilon}$ on $\Fpx$ has image $(\p-1)/d$ and loss factor $d=\gcd(\varepsilon,\p-1)$, every nonempty fibre of size $d$ ($\varepsilon=1,2,3,4,6,12$ on $\F_{13}$).
p08035.source: Props. 9, 10

p08036.statement: Cayley propagators and boost transports have loss factor one: the wave dynamics is isentropic, compression confined to the power-map layer.
p08036.source: Cors. 6, 7

p08037.statement: Period dichotomy: kinetic Hamiltonians are nilpotent, fully admissible, with unipotent propagators of order $\p$; potential Hamiltonians give diagonal propagators with phases in $N^{1}$ and order dividing $\p+1$ ($14$ at $13$, $18$ at $17$); the mixed datum $\operatorname{ord}(U)=1563$ at $\p=5$; composites take the lcm ($13,14\mapsto182$); the three tori $C_{\p-1}$, $C_\p$, $C_{\p+1}$ each govern one dynamical role.
p08037.source: Thm. 8, Cor. 8, Rem. 14

p08038.statement: The four domains of one framed shell: the additive Fourier pair on the meridians $M_0$ (space) and $M_\kap$ (momentum), the multiplicative pair on the latitudes $L_1$ (time) and $L_{\kap+1}$ (energy); zonal and meridional motion; both dualities the index advance by the capacity.
p08038.source: § 7, Fig. 2

p08039.statement: The latitude identities: $\kap+1$ is the first rung past the midpoint of the ladder $1,\dots,2\kap$; $m\mapsto m+\kap$ is multiplication by $g^{\kap}=\pm\im$ and $a\mapsto a+\kap$ sends $1$ to $\kap+1$; $\kap=-4^{-1}$ so the energy radius is $3\cdot4^{-1}$; $\pi=2\kap=-2^{-1}=-c^{2}$, on the Carrier $\pi_\Omega=2S$; the unit-norm circle has $\p-1$ points. On $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$ and the laboratory Carrier.
p08039.source: § 7

p08040.statement: The free evolution is the drive: the pullback $D\psi(x)=\psi(g^{-1}x)$ is unitary, the characters $\chi_k$ are its eigenvectors with $D\chi_k=g^{-k}\chi_k$, and every character line is isotropic except $k=0,(\p-1)/2$ with eigenvalues $\pm1=N^{1}\cap\mu_{\p-1}$. Exhaustive on $\F_{13}$, $\F_{17}$.
p08040.source: Thm. 9

p08041.statement: Two evolution sectors, one space: the split-phase sector of the drive and the norm-one sector of the Cayley propagators meet in $\{\pm1\}$ alone ($\operatorname{ord}(g^{-1})=\p-1$); the cycle Laplacian $\Delta_\Phi=D+D^{-1}-2I$ is self-adjoint, its Cayley steps commute with $D$ and the composite is unitary ($\p=13$); the dispersion relation $-\Delta_\Phi\chi_k=(2-g^{k}-g^{-k})\chi_k$; no meridional plane waves ($\gcd(\p,|K^{\times}|)=1$); $\mathcal D^{s}-m$ invertible for $m\ne0$, so mass is an evolution phase, not a kernel condition.
p08041.source: Cor. 9, § 7

p08042.statement: The shell reading: Schrödinger dynamics is the exact zonal evolution (the drive on $L_1$, its spectrum the winding ladder at $L_{\kap+1}$), Dirac dynamics the exact meridional development, the three tori the three dynamical seats ($C_{\p-1}$ free evolution, $C_\p$ translations and kinetic periods, $C_{\p+1}$ interactions and boosts), the light cone a square-class boundary. Falsifier: a registered dynamics of the shell requiring a phase outside the two tori, or a mass without winding (D13).
p08042.source: Rem. 15

p08046.statement: The classification of the admissible set $\calA(H)$ for a general self-adjoint Hamiltonian — the roots of $\det(I-\alpha H)$ in $K^{-}$ — beyond the nilpotent case ($\calA=K^{-}$, C6, E4) and the diagonal case (the Cayley transform of the spectrum, C5).

p10001.statement: The framed substrate: the Subject shell $\Fp(\chron;0,1,\gen)$ with $\p=4\kap+1$, the derived quarter-turn $\im=-\gen^{\kap}$, the phase cycle $4\kap=2\pi=\p-1$, the framed-complex labels; the Carrier $\Car$ of cardinality $\Om=4\dS+1$ with its admissibility congruences; the realisation doctrine (a row stating what a physical term denotes, defended by its consequences and killed by its falsifier).
p10001.source: [Akhtman 2025; Akhtman 2026; Akhtman 2025; Akhtman & Voether 2026]

p10002.statement: The holographic principle as the count: the capacity $\dS$ is the de Sitter entropy, the finite number of physical states behind the observer’s horizon, the one imported number of the paper.
p10002.source: [Bekenstein 1973; 't Hooft 1993; Susskind 1995; Gibbons & Hawking 1977]

p10003.statement: The shell Fourier structure: on $\Fp^{\Phi}$, $\Phi=C_{\p-1}$, the matrix $W_{jk}=\gen^{jk}$, the normalized operator $F=\im W$ with $F^{2}=J$, $F^{4}=I$, and the fractional family with its cardinal skeleton $\{0,\kap,2\kap,3\kap\}$.
p10003.source: [Akhtman 2026]; Rem. 6

p10004.statement: Classical dimensional analysis and the Planck units: the $\Pi$-theorem, the free-abelian exponent group of $M$-$L$-$T$, Planck’s construction of the natural units from $\{c,\hbar,G\}$, and the observation that only dimensionless ratios of constants are measurable.
p10004.source: [Buckingham 1914; Bridgman 1922; Barenblatt 1996; Planck 1899; Duff et al. 2002; Uzan 2003]

p10005.statement: The registrability hierarchy of the framework: coherent registration bounded at $\sqrt\p$, read on the exponent lattice as the coherence window $2\sqrt\kap=\sqrt{\p-1}$; the finite-field algebra of square classes and cyclic groups used throughout.
p10005.source: [Akhtman 2026; Lidl & Niederreiter 1997]; Rem. 19

p10006.statement: The Unruh and Hawking temperature forms, $T_U=\hbar a/2\pi c\,k_B$, as the shape the temperature domain closes on.
p10006.source: [Unruh 1976; Hawking 1975]
